title: Why Dating Isn’t Just About Feelings
paragraphs:
Why Dating Isn’t Just About Feelings
When Butterflies Fade, Truth Remains

You thought it was love because your heart raced, your hands trembled, and your thoughts kept drifting back to them in quiet moments. You called it “something real” because it felt intense… alive… almost divine.
But no one warned you how easily feelings can impersonate purpose.
No one told you that what feels right can still lead you far away from what is righteous.
And now you’re here… wondering why something that felt so beautiful is leaving your spirit restless.
Be honest. This hit harder than you expected.
Because deep down, you already know… dating was never supposed to be just about feelings.

In Scripture, love is never defined by emotion first. It is defined by truth, commitment, and obedience. The Greek word used in 1 Corinthians 13 is “ἀγάπη” (agápē), a love that is not rooted in shifting emotions but in sacrificial, covenantal action.

“Ἡ ἀγάπη μακροθυμεῖ, χρηστεύεται…”
Love suffers long and is kind.
It doesn’t say love feels good all the time. It says love endures.
And that changes everything.
Because what you’ve been calling “love” might just be chemistry without covenant.
What you’ve been chasing might be emotional intensity without spiritual alignment.
And that’s where so many hearts quietly break.
Not because love failed…
…but because it was never built on truth.

The Hebrew language gives us another layer of depth. The word often used for love in covenantal context is “חֶסֶד” (chesed), meaning steadfast love, loyal love, a love that binds itself even when feelings fluctuate.
That’s not the kind of love modern dating teaches.
Modern dating says, “Follow your heart.”
But Scripture warns you.
“The heart is deceitful above all things…” (Jeremiah 17:9)
In Hebrew, “עָקֹב הַלֵּב” (aqov halev) literally means twisted, unreliable, even treacherous.
So why are we trusting something God already told us is broken?
This is where it gets uncomfortable.
Because if dating isn’t about feelings… then it’s about something far more serious.
It’s about alignment with God’s will.
It’s about guarding your soul.
It’s about asking a question most people avoid:
“Is this drawing me closer to Christ… or slowly pulling me away?”
You can feel deeply for someone… and still be walking into spiritual compromise.
You can laugh together, pray together, even talk about God together… and still be unequally yoked.
And that’s not just a phrase.
In 2 Corinthians 6:14, the Greek says:

“Μὴ γίνεσθε ἑτεροζυγοῦντες…”
Do not become unequally yoked.
“ἑτεροζυγοῦντες” (heterozygountes) paints a picture of two animals bound together but pulling in different directions.
It’s exhausting.
It’s painful.
And eventually… something breaks.
Sometimes it’s the relationship.
Sometimes it’s your peace.
Sometimes it’s your intimacy with God.
And that’s the part no one posts about.
Because it’s easier to show the highlight reels than to confess the quiet conviction.
This isn’t about condemning you.
This is about waking you up.
Because Jesus didn’t die just to forgive your sins.
He died to transform your desires.
Even in dating.
Especially in dating.

The Aramaic expression of love carries this weight too. In the language Jesus often spoke, love isn’t shallow affection. It’s relational commitment, deeply tied to faithfulness and truth. When Jesus restored Peter in John 21, He used layered language, asking:

“Σίμων… ἀγαπᾷς με;”
Simon… do you love Me?
Not “do you feel something for Me?”
But “are you devoted to Me?”
That’s the standard.
And if we’re honest… many relationships today couldn’t answer that question.
Because they were built on attraction, not devotion.
On vibes, not vision.
On feelings, not foundation.
But here’s the grace.
God is not standing over you in disappointment.
He’s calling you back into alignment.
Back into truth.
Back into a love that actually reflects Him.
Because the Gospel is not just about saving your soul.
It’s about rewriting your story.
Yes, even your dating life.
Especially your dating life.
From scandal… to grace.
From confusion… to clarity.
From emotional chaos… to Christ-centered conviction.
That’s what Jesus does.
He rewrites everything.
So if you’ve been hurt, misled, or confused in relationships…
If you’ve called something “love” that left you spiritually empty…
If you’ve ignored conviction just to keep someone close…
You’re not too far gone.
But you do need to decide.
Will you keep following your feelings…
Or will you start following Christ?
And if you know someone who’s stuck in a relationship that’s pulling them away from God, don’t stay silent. It might be the wake-up call they’ve been avoiding but desperately need.
And if you’re serious about growing deeper, about disciplining your heart, about understanding Scripture beyond surface-level inspiration… step into something deeper.
If you truly want to glorify God… don’t just consume truth.
Carry it.
Live it.
Because one day, you’ll realize…

it was never just about who you were dating…
it was always about who was shaping your soul.
